jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Schoolhouse

Founded by Sal Khan, Schoolhouse is a peer-to-peer learning platform that delivers human connection and develops durable skills through online learning to best prepare students to thrive in the age of AI. So far, we’ve reached 200k+ learners from 180+ countries and we plan to grow to millions.

About the Vision

Our vision is to provide an education safety net to ensure that no talent goes undiscovered and that every student feels empowered in our changing world. We do this by bringing high school students together around learning to create an environment where they can develop and showcase academic mastery and durable skills.

At Schoolhouse, learning is academic, civic, and global. Students join tutoring sessions where peers help them reach academic goals through personalized support. They participate in Dialogues to discuss challenging issues and empathize across divides. Above all, students belong to a global community centered around human connection.

We believe this vision is ambitious, so we need a team that can move quickly in the face of ambiguity. We work with sincerity and empathy and believe deeply in the power of human connection. We step in to help each other out, we think big but start small, we uplift each other, and we’re all learners at heart.

Learn more about our vision and our values here:

  • Schoolhouse TED Talk

  • Teen Helps 52-Year-Old Man Earn His High School Diploma

  • Schoolhouse’s Public Roadmap

  • What are Schoolhouse's community values?

About the Role

We're looking for a Chief of Staff to take our ambitious 2028 vision and launch the key systems, projects, and partnerships that get us there.

This is a rare generalist role for someone who wants to operate at the center of a fast-growing nonprofit that is already the largest free human tutoring organization in the world. You'll have genuine exposure to leaders across the education ecosystem — from Sal Khan and board members like Arne Duncan to partners like College Board and Google Gemini — and the opportunity to put their reach to work for students.

Reporting to the President, you'll take our most important 0-to-1 bets from idea to early traction, represent Schoolhouse to our most important stakeholders, and run the operating rhythm that keeps the organization on track. The work touches nearly every part of the organization and it will evolve as we do.

You'll own three things:

  • Strategic projects. Lead high-impact, 0-to-1 projects that advance our 2028 vision like fundraising or growth strategy. Run validation experiments, read the signal honestly, and build the case for whether to scale into a full initiative, pivot the approach, or cut it entirely.

  • External relations. Serve as a trusted liaison for high-stakes partners, donors, and stakeholders. Understand and articulate our goals and vision clearly, judge how a new partner or project fits our ecosystem and resourcing, and turn that into recommendations for the relationships we should cultivate and secure.

  • Business operations. Run the operating rhythm of the organization and the follow-through that turns decisions into outcomes. Support critical work across HR, legal, and finance, and drive the people operations that keep us healthy, like hiring processes and our biannual team retreats.

Some examples of what this could look like in your first year:

  • Design and pilot a suite of new fundraising channels, then write the roadmap that decides which channels we scale and how

  • Run point on a new organizational growth partnership (akin to the College Board) from first conversation through scoping, agreement, and pilot launch

  • Revamp an existing operational workflow, like our term planning or hiring process, into an improved version that the whole team uses

  • Plan two company retreats end to end, from strategic objectives to agenda to logistics

About You

If this sounds like you, we'd love for you to apply!

  • At least 5+ years in a Chief of Staff, operating, or strategy role — as a founder / early operator at a high-growth startup or in a consulting / banking / strategy role with hands-on operating experience since.

  • You've helped take something from 0 to 1: a new program, product, or partnership.

  • You thrive in high ambiguity. You can take a vague, high-stakes problem with no clear owner and turn it into a plan, momentum, and a result.

  • You shine in external, high-stakes settings and have operated closely with executives. Your writing and speaking are high-polish, and you can represent Schoolhouse credibly to a funder, a partner, or the whole team.

  • You're high-output across both breadth and depth. You context-switch without dropping balls, create clarity amid the noise, and build high-quality things fast.

  • You are an exceptional communicator who builds trusted relationships easily — internally across every function, and externally with partners and stakeholders.

  • You have sound judgment about people and priorities, and the discretion to handle sensitive situations well.

  • You have a strong ownership mentality. You fill gaps, ask for help when you need it, and follow through without being managed.

  • You're available to work in a US timezone.

Bonus points

  • You have experience with fundraising, development, or board and donor relations.

  • You have experience in education, ed-tech, or another mission-driven organization.

Life at Schoolhouse

  • Work with an amazing team. We’ve got folks with backgrounds in education, consulting, astrophysics, startups, and more.

  • Fully remote with flexible working hours. Meetings are in US Pacific Time mornings.

  • Take real time off. We have unlimited PTO & use it. Folks regularly take time off throughout the year.

  • Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits. Work-from-home stipend. Professional development budget. Health, dental, vision (for US employees).

  • Semesterly retreats and monthly regional meetups

  • Make an impact you can see. Check out our community stories page. Watch students help each other learn. See tutors grow into leaders. Your will help real people learn and grow.

About the Application Process

We might make some adjustments, but our previous interview process has consisted of:

  • A 30 minute intro call

  • A 45 minute hiring manager interview

  • A 45 minute strategy case with the leadership team

  • A 45 minute panel-style discussion with team members across functions

  • Reference calls

 

We’re building an inclusive and equitable platform for learners across the world, and it’s important our core team reflects these principles too. We strongly encourage people from underrepresented groups apply!

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Schoolhouse

Founded by Sal Khan, Schoolhouse is a peer-to-peer learning platform that delivers human connection and develops durable skills through online learning to best prepare students to thrive in the age of AI. So far, we’ve reached 200k+ learners from 180+ countries and we plan to grow to millions.

About the Vision

Our vision is to provide an education safety net to ensure that no talent goes undiscovered and that every student feels empowered in our changing world. We do this by bringing high school students together around learning to create an environment where they can develop and showcase academic mastery and durable skills.

At Schoolhouse, learning is academic, civic, and global. Students join tutoring sessions where peers help them reach academic goals through personalized support. They participate in Dialogues to discuss challenging issues and empathize across divides. Above all, students belong to a global community centered around human connection.

We believe this vision is ambitious, so we need a team that can move quickly in the face of ambiguity. We value sincerity and empathy and believe deeply in the power of human connection. We step in to help each other out, we think big but start small, we uplift each other, and we’re all learners at heart.

Learn more about our vision and our values here:

  • Teen Helps 52-Year-Old Man Earn His High School Diploma

  • The Power of Peer Tutoring

  • Schoolhouse’s Public Roadmap

  • What are Schoolhouse's community values?

About the Role

We’re looking for Senior Software Engineers who want to build stuff that’ll have an impact. You’ll join our 5-person engineering team and own full-stack features that hundreds of thousands of learners and tutors use worldwide.

Engineers at Schoolhouse have lots of ownership — you’ll work directly with our designer and other stakeholders to build out new experiments and streamline existing operations. We think the best way for engineers to build a quality product is to be involved early, drive progress, and stay close to our end users.

Scaling free quality interactions between students around the world comes with challenges that live at the intersection of UX, people ops, and technology. We need to both meet learner / tutor needs while ensuring that these interactions stay high quality and safe.

Some examples of what we’ve worked on include:

  • Building an AI simulation & coach to help tutors practice for their first tutoring session

  • Experimenting with new ways to connect tutors to learners wanting immediate homework help

  • Creating a moderation system to automatically recognize and act on safety issues so humans can focus their time on the most important issues

Responsibilities

  • Work with users and teammates to define problems, contribute product ideas, and lead work from prototypes / experiments through deployment.

  • Break ambiguous work into manageable steps, coordinating contributions when needed

  • Write simple, readable code and create / improve patterns that make future work easier.

  • Help teammates grow through code reviews and pairing sessions

About You

If this sounds like you, we’d love for you to apply!

  • [Senior] You’ve been a full-stack software engineer 3+ years and have a track record of leading full-stack projects from ambiguous problem through launch and iteration.

  • [Senior] You can anticipate risks and make decisions that balance tradeoffs between speed, quality, and user experience.

  • You have experience with Typescript, Node.js, React, Next.js, and Postgres (or can ramp up quickly).

  • You build for users & have a nose for understanding what would help them the most.

  • You move quickly while maintaining code quality. Perfect is the enemy of good.

  • You fill in the gaps — you ask for help, but still work independently to figure things out. If necessary you can put on another hat if it’ll help users the most.

  • You’re available to work in a US timezone.

Bonus points

  • You have deep technical experience with our stack Typescript, Node.js, React, Next.js, Postgres, AWS, and GCP.

  • You have experience building mobile apps.

  • You have experience working in education or on an ed-tech product.

Life at Schoolhouse

  • Work with an amazing team. We’ve got folks with backgrounds in education, consulting, astrophysics, startups, and more.

  • Fully remote with flexible working hours. Meetings are in US Pacific Time mornings.

  • Take real time off. We have unlimited PTO & use it. Folks regularly take time off throughout the year.

  • Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits. Work-from-home stipend. Professional development budget. Health, dental, vision (for US employees).

  • Semesterly retreats and monthly regional meetups

  • Make an impact you can see. Check out our community stories page. Watch students help each other learn. See tutors grow into leaders. Your code will help real people learn and grow.

About the Application Process

  • We might make some adjustments, but our expected interview process:

  • A 30-minute intro screen to learn more about you and understand whether this role is a mutual fit

  • A 45-minute screen where you'll read some code and brainstorm / prioritize product ideas

  • A 1-hour programming interview where you’ll fix bugs and implement features on a toy repo

  • A 1-hour systems design problem where you'll design a data model / api and handle challenges at scale

  • A 45-minute culture fit call with non-technical team members

  • Reference calls

 

We’re building an inclusive and equitable platform for learners across the world, and it’s important our core team reflects these principles too. Research shows people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we strongly encourage to you apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.

ABOUT THE APPLICATION PROCESS

 - We might make some adjustments, but our expected interview process:

 - A 30-minute intro screen to learn more about you and understand whether this role is a mutual fit

 - A 45-minute screen where you'll read some code and brainstorm / prioritize product ideas

 - A 1-hour programming interview where you’ll fix bugs and implement features on a toy repo

 - A 1-hour systems design problem where you'll design a data model / api and handle challenges at scale

 - A 45-minute culture fit call with non-technical team members

 - Reference calls

 

We’re building an inclusive and equitable platform for learners across the world, and it’s important our core team reflects these principles too. Research shows people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we strongly encourage to you apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.
